## For teachers

Each case asks whether a particular STACK answer test accepts a submitted
answer. This report shows which cases STACK SymPy can check, where its result
agrees with STACK, and where a teacher should expect a difference.

### How to read the results

**Port** means STACK SymPy. **STACK** means the reference Moodle/Maxima answer
test. **Expected** is the outcome recorded in the original case. Green can
mean that a wrong answer was correctly rejected. A matching result for one
case does not establish that every question using that test behaves identically.

State the mathematical domain, distinguish written form from value, and use
numerical tests for approximate answers. The [semantics discussions for STACK authors](semantics.qmd#author-attention) record the detailed conventions and unresolved questions. Start with the
[authoring guide](../docs/authoring.html) when preparing a question, and run its
own tests as well as inspecting the examples. [Python answer tests for matrix tasks](../docs/python-checker-api.html)
are documented separately from this native comparison.

<div class="status-legend" aria-label="How to read the colors">
  <span class="tone-good">Green: expected behavior or agreement</span>
  <span class="tone-notice">Amber: known issue or explained difference</span>
  <span class="tone-bad">Red: unexpected result</span>
  <span class="tone-neutral">Gray: not graded, outside scope, or unavailable</span>
</div>

## For developers

### Scope and interpretation

The inventory contains 2,303 imported answer-test cases. It compares CAS
functions, not complete Moodle grading sessions. The port currently provides
ten native-compatible answer-test families. Unsupported cases remain visible
by missing test or input feature; some direct STACK calls require parser or
controller preparation and are not compared.

“Test applicability” asks whether a test can compare the supplied values. It
is separate from syntax validity and the accept/reject mark. Form tests may
reject equivalent expressions. Browser agreement includes invalid/unsupported
classifications as well as graded results; the summary distinguishes them.

Source codes `0` and `1` request rejection and acceptance; `-1` requests a
controlled error. Codes `-2` and `-3` flag source-authored native deviations.
Only reviewed cases receive the “Known STACK issue” label. Ordinary notes are
retained but not generally compared; asserted controlled-error notes are
checked separately.

The Python-only `PythonChecker` test, including its supplied basis and matrix
property functions, does not increase the native inventory or its coverage
counts. Its authored, unit and browser checks establish separate Python
behavior. See the
[developer reference](../docs/python-checker-api.html#for-developers).

### Saved evidence and reproduction

The detailed [conventions reference](semantics.qmd) records
case-specific reasoning, sources and open questions. The
[development guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy#supported-subset-and-grading-behavior)
explains how to reproduce the reports. A normal website render reads the
saved results; it does not rerun STACK comparisons.
